perspective:
Ethan’s accessible information:

- He is Ethan Mohamud, a plumber, and Gary Guo is his close, long-time friend from middle school. Ethan knows Gary is a doctor and that they rely on each other for support.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep. He felt concerned and invited Gary to a weekend relaxation/rejuvenation retreat, telling him his health matters and that two days might give him a new perspective. Gary declined, saying he appreciated it but had too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more than just professional obligation. He told Gary they had been friends since middle school, that Gary could tell him anything, and that he was there to help, not judge. Gary said it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan.
- Afterward, Gary opened up to Ethan about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan felt relief and empathy and suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed and said he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in, discussed Gary’s progress and remaining challenges, saw Gary making efforts to change, felt hopeful and proud, and continued encouraging him. Gary told him things were better, that Ethan’s help made him less overwhelmed, and that he had time for a movie.
- After a year, Ethan saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance on his own. He felt satisfied and happy, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away and knew Gary had this. Gary thanked him, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and felt more in control.
